metadata.scope: Focused research review for 40 ms speech IMF fitting and learned VMD; not a formal exhaustive systematic review.
metadata.search: Publisher proceedings and journals, author preprints and institutional manuscripts; backward/forward title searches; emphasis on 2024–2026 and essential older foundations.
metadata.verification: Publication year follows the cited conference/journal issue or early-access publication, not the year embedded in a DOI or the first preprint. Primary sources support technical summaries; full proof audits and reproductions were not performed.
metadata.evidence: Per-paper evidence field distinguishes abstract/metadata screening from methodological sections inspected.
metadata.exclusions: Generic VMD+predictor application papers were not treated as learned decomposition. Unverified conference acceptances were not promoted from arXiv to a published venue.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Density-Based Adaptive Mode Decomposition
papers.authors: Hao Jia; Chunyu Yang; Cesar F. Caiafa; Zhe Sun; Feng Duan; Jordi Solé-Casals
papers.finding: Relates VMD optimization to density clustering; introduces automatic mode detection, direct extraction, and selective variational refinement.
papers.proposed_application: Compare automatic mode-count/center initialization with fixed K; initialize a learned decomposition from spectral clusters.
papers.limitation: Adaptivity and speech reconstruction do not establish corpus-trained decomposition or compact formula descriptions.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Short-time variational mode decomposition
papers.authors: Hao Jia et al.
papers.finding: Extends bandwidth minimization to windowed time-frequency data; dynamic variant permits time-varying center frequencies.
papers.proposed_application: Use as the short-time and moving-frequency baseline; distinguish independent window VMD from its window-coupled objective.
papers.limitation: Reported application is EEG; it does not establish speech compression. Publisher also lists a corrigendum whose scope should be checked before reproduction.
papers.year_note: Journal issue January 2026; available online July 2025.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: TFD-Net: Towards Intelligent Time-Frequency Mode Decomposition with Practical Applications
papers.authors: Pingping Pan; Yunjian Zhang; Jinyi Liu
papers.finding: Combines a physically motivated time-frequency encoder with query-based mode extraction to learn separation of nonstationary components.
papers.proposed_application: A strong neural decomposition baseline and a source of mode-query and ridge-learning ideas.
papers.limitation: A learned mode extractor is not itself a compact mathematical expression generator or speech codec.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: C-EMDNet: A Nonlinear Morphological Deep Framework for Robust Speech Enhancement
papers.authors: Kais Khaldi; Sahar Almenwer; Afrah Alanazi; Inam Alanazi; Anis Mohamed
papers.finding: Uses a U-Net to estimate masks over a CEEMDAN time-IMF representation.
papers.proposed_application: Useful control demonstrating that learning masks on adaptive modes differs from learning the decomposition itself.
papers.limitation: Its described CEEMDAN front end is a decomposition stage; the paper does not demonstrate gradients through CEEMDAN or parameter-vector coding.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Plug-and-play learnable EMD module for time-domain speech separation
papers.authors: Xiaokang Yang; Wenjun Ke; Jianguo Wei
papers.finding: Constructs a learnable EMD-inspired module, using neural operations to replace conventional envelope computation.
papers.proposed_application: A direct speech-specific comparison for learned decomposition rather than only downstream processing of fixed modes.
papers.limitation: Speech separation is the objective, not low-description-length IMF fitting; full text was not available in this review.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Variational generalized nonlinear mode decomposition: Algorithm and applications
papers.authors: Hongbing Wang; Shiqian Chen; Wanming Zhai
papers.finding: Combines time-frequency fusion, ridge-based mode-type identification and variational recovery of chirp and dispersive components.
papers.proposed_application: Test whether speech transients need localized/dispersive components alongside oscillatory ones.
papers.limitation: Its mode-type discrimination is an engineered procedure, not unrestricted learned function synthesis.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Data-driven adaptive chirp mode decomposition with application to machine fault diagnosis under non-stationary conditions
papers.authors: Hongbing Wang; Shiqian Chen; Wanming Zhai
papers.finding: Builds instantaneous-frequency initialization and recursive extraction for nonstationary chirp components.
papers.proposed_application: Compare demodulation and IF initialization against fitting raw oscillating IMFs.
papers.limitation: Data-driven here means signal-adaptive estimation; it does not mean a model trained across a speech corpus.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Adaptive Variational Nonlinear Chirp Mode Decomposition
papers.authors: Hao Liang; Xinghao Ding; Andreas Jakobsson; Xiaotong Tu; Yue Huang
papers.finding: Bayesian adaptation estimates amplitude/frequency trajectories and the active dictionary, reducing bandwidth-parameter dependence.
papers.proposed_application: Investigate learned bandwidths, uncertainty, and automatic component activity instead of fixing eight equal-budget modes.
papers.limitation: Bayesian signal adaptation is distinct from neural amortization; compact coefficient coding still has to be added.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract and author-hosted methodological excerpt

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Learnable Empirical Mode Decomposition based on Mathematical Morphology
papers.authors: Santiago Velasco-Forero; Romain Pagès; Jesús Angulo
papers.finding: Learns EMD-like envelope operations using mathematical morphology, including learned structuring functions and envelope combinations.
papers.proposed_application: A principled alternative decomposition module if differentiable VMD proves too restrictive.
papers.limitation: Demonstrations concern hyperspectral classification, not compact speech synthesis.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Nonlinear Chirp Mode Decomposition: A Variational Method
papers.authors: Shiqian Chen et al.
papers.finding: Uses demodulation to handle chirps whose bandwidth makes standard VMD assumptions restrictive.
papers.proposed_application: A mathematical foundation for replacing constant centers with trajectories.
papers.limitation: Trajectories are not automatically low-dimensional coefficient vectors; decomposition and compact fitting remain separate.

papers.group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
papers.title: Variational Mode Decomposition
papers.authors: Konstantin Dragomiretskiy; Dominique Zosso
papers.finding: Jointly extracts modes by minimizing their bandwidth after demodulation, subject to signal reconstruction.
papers.proposed_application: Keep its constrained objective as the reference when deciding what a learned VMD module should preserve.
papers.limitation: Small bandwidth is not a theorem of small polynomial degree or short symbolic description.

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
papers.title: Variable Projection algorithms: Theoretical insights and a novel approach for problems with large residual
papers.authors: Guangyong Chen; Peng Xue; Min Gan; Jing Chen; Wenzhong Guo; C. L. Philip Chen
papers.finding: Studies local convergence of variable projection and proposes VPLR for separable nonlinear problems with appreciable residuals.
papers.proposed_application: Eliminate linear amplitude coefficients by least squares while optimizing only nonlinear frequencies/shape parameters.
papers.limitation: Applicable only where parameters enter conditionally linearly; it does not solve arbitrary symbolic topology search or guarantee global optimality.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract and author-preprint formulation/Jacobian sections inspected

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
papers.title: Weighted Hermite Variable Projection Networks for Classifying Visually Evoked Potentials
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
papers.authors: Tamás Dózsa; Carl Böck; Jens Meier; Péter Kovács
papers.finding: Introduces a differentiable variable-projection representation with trainable weighted Hermite functions.
papers.proposed_application: A concrete example of backpropagation through a fitted function representation; transfer the mechanism to oscillatory atoms.
papers.limitation: Hermite functions and EEG classification are its chosen setting; speech and unrestricted formulas need separate validation.

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
papers.title: Differentiable Time-Varying Linear Prediction in the Context of End-to-End Analysis-by-Synthesis
papers.authors: Chin-Yun Yu; György Fazekas
papers.finding: Makes sample-wise time-varying linear prediction differentiable and efficient in an analysis-by-synthesis voice system.
papers.proposed_application: A structured speech baseline and guidance for learning parameters through the actual resynthesis operation.
papers.limitation: Source-filter voice synthesis does not demonstrate compact representations of arbitrary VMD modes.

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
papers.title: Sinusoidal Frequency Estimation by Gradient Descent
papers.authors: Ben Hayes; Charalampos Saitis; György Fazekas
papers.finding: Uses a complex-exponential surrogate and Wirtinger gradients to improve frequency optimization despite highly nonconvex sinusoidal losses.
papers.proposed_application: Test this against direct real-frequency least squares on known tones/chirps before rejecting a generated oscillatory expression.
papers.limitation: Its demonstrated sinusoidal setting does not guarantee recovery of general AM-FM or arbitrary nested expressions.
papers.evidence: Author-hosted introduction and surrogate/Jacobian sections inspected

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves

papers.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing
papers.authors: Shayan Aziznejad; Thomas Debarre; Michael Unser

papers.proposed_application: Use an optimized sparse curve representation as a well-defined reference against unconstrained symbolic search.
papers.limitation: Optimality is for its specified variational problem; it is not global optimality among all waveform functions.
papers.evidence: Author-hosted abstract and variational formulations inspected

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
papers.title: Coupled Splines for Sparse Curve Fitting
papers.authors: Icíar Lloréns Jover; Thomas Debarre; Shayan Aziznejad; Michael Unser
papers.finding: Uses sparsity-promoting variational curve fitting and complementary spline components with controlled smoothness.
papers.proposed_application: Transfer adaptive knot allocation and mixed-smoothness modeling to IMF envelopes or residual phase.
papers.limitation: The paper addresses closed image contours; its theorems cannot simply be claimed for speech waveforms.

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
papers.title: Learning Activation Functions in Deep (Spline) Neural Networks
papers.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing
papers.authors: Pakshal Bohra; Joaquim Campos; Harshit Gupta; Shayan Aziznejad; Michael Unser
papers.finding: Learns free-form activation shapes using spline parameterizations and second-order total-variation regularization.
papers.proposed_application: An alternative to treating sine/SnakeBeta as the only activation choices; count learned knots and coefficients explicitly.
papers.limitation: Free-form activation learning still has a representation and regularization prior; it is not automatic minimal symbolic expression discovery.

papers.group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
papers.title: Separable nonlinear least squares: the variable projection method and its applications
papers.authors: Gene H. Golub; Victor Pereyra
papers.finding: Reviews elimination of conditionally linear parameters in nonlinear least-squares fitting.
papers.proposed_application: The foundational explanation for separating amplitude fitting from oscillatory shape/frequency fitting.
papers.limitation: A numerical optimization reference, not evidence that a particular speech representation is sufficient.

synthesis: Main finding

The most useful direction is to learn a decomposition whose modes have cheap, accurately fitted function descriptions. Standard VMD minimizes demodulated bandwidth; that objective is not the same as minimizing the number of coefficients or expression tokens needed to reproduce each mode. This is a proposed connection between the decomposition and fitting literature, not a result demonstrated by the listed papers.
Three meanings of data-driven

Signal-adaptive numerical decomposition (VMD, DD-ACMD, DAMD), learning a downstream model on precomputed modes (e.g. mode masks), and a corpus-trained differentiable decomposition are distinct. Our intended second experiment needs the third, trained against the measured consequences of function fitting. A paper using VMD before an LSTM does not establish this.
Oscillation structure versus polynomial degree

A rapidly oscillating mode can be described more economically through an envelope and phase than by a polynomial of its waveform. Test direct expression discovery against factorized amplitude/phase expression discovery; do not force every real mode into one AM-FM template. Chirp-aware decomposition and localized oscillatory components are useful alternatives to constant-center VMD. Zero crossings alone do not specify the required polynomial degree or numerical conditioning.
Continuous fitting before judging expression quality

For a candidate sum of nonlinear atoms, fit conditionally linear coefficients by least squares and optimize only the nonlinear shape parameters when the structure permits. Compare variable projection, robust multi-start nonlinear fitting, and the complex sinusoidal surrogate on controlled signals. A poor local fit is not evidence that the generated function cannot represent the mode.
Expression generation should include refinement

RAG-SR, neural MCTS and TPSR suggest retaining successful expressions, editing subtrees and using numerical fitting feedback during search. This is better motivated than relying solely on independent samples from a small pretrained sequence model. SymFormer/E2E motivate learning constant initialization too. Keep equal-budget random and search baselines to establish that learning contributes.
Learned shapes are not automatically symbolic formulas

KAN, sparse splines, SIREN, WIRE and FINER++ offer flexible curve models. They answer a useful capacity question, but their parameters include all required weights, knots and coefficients. A learned activation is not itself a short analytic expression. Symbolification is an additional approximation whose error and description size must be measured.
A practical joint experiment

Start with fixed VMD and validated per-mode fits. Next compare an unfolded VMD module, a chirp-aware variant, and a learned filter-bank control. Use per-mode bandwidth/center parameters and learnable activity gates. A first outer objective can combine waveform error after formula evaluation, complete expression-description cost, and constraints/regularization preserving the intended narrow-band mode interpretation. Do not supervise only the sum of unfitted sampled modes.
Discrete structures and differentiable training

For a fixed expression structure, unrolled or implicit differentiation can propagate through continuous coefficient fitting subject to regularity and solver accuracy. Changing expression topology is discrete. Use alternating symbolic search and decomposition updates, or validate a learned cost-to-fit surrogate against actual search outcomes. Calling the whole mixed discrete/continuous system differentiable would be inaccurate without specifying this mechanism.
Measure what must actually be stored

Record floating coefficient count, expression-tree/DAG structure, knot positions, precision, any per-clip mode metadata, and the residual description. Shared model assets are separate. Parameters eliminated from numerical optimization are still parameters to store. A learned mode count should be penalized through realized description cost; equally splitting coefficients across all modes is only a baseline.
Proposed ablations

Decomposition: fixed VMD, learned-bandwidth VMD, chirp-aware decomposition, structured learned filter bank. Fitting: direct expression search, amplitude/phase expression search, sparse spline/KAN capacity control. Optimization: ordinary multi-start, variable projection where separable, oscillatory surrogate. Search: random, pretrained-only, online retrieval/mutation. Budget: adaptive versus equal mode allocation. Evaluate each change at matched expression-description budgets and comparable search time.
Validation and limits

Use known-answer functions with increasing modulation/transient complexity; measure topology recovery, constant-fitting success and final waveform errors separately. On speech, keep speakers disjoint for learning but allow all samples of a test IMF when fitting that IMF. Report mean/median, threshold success and the error/size frontier. Perceptual conclusions require later whole-speech evaluation and listening; separation metrics do not become valid for a 40 ms IMF merely because they produce frame-level outputs.
What this review does not establish

The reviewed sources provide components of the proposed system. I did not verify a published paper demonstrating the exact combination of 40 ms speech, a corpus-trained VMD-like decomposition, generated per-mode expressions and an objective charging the complete stored description. That is a scoped search finding, not a novelty claim or a proof that such a paper does not exist.
